newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends at highs on commercials, rain.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends at highs on commercials, rain.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on commercial demand and harvest-delaying, crop-downgrading rains in Alberta, traders said.

"Talk some elevator companies offered premiums in the country late in the day pushed the market higher," a trader said. Jan-Mar spread at $1, Nov-Jan $4, Nov-July $7, Nov-Mar $5. Volume was 5,230 lots, or 104,600 tonnes, with 700 hedges.
November canola rose $1.20 to $437.60 and January ended up $0.80 to $441.10.
October flax rose $0.40 to $397.20, November up $0.50 to $372 on commercial demand. Oct-Jan at $20.50. Volume 235.
Locals sold five October oats up US$0.50 to US$123.50.
October feed wheat lost $1.60 to $198.90 on talk rain in Alberta will produce more feed wheat. Oct-Mar spread at $17, Oct-Dec $13. Volume was 1,550 lots.

November western barley rose $2.10 to $150.40 and February was up $2.40 to $155.10 on Alberta Wheat Pool short covering and feedlot buying, traders said. November barley to October feed wheat spread at $50. Volume was 1,600 lots.
PCTS sold October peas up US$1 to US$210.50 to Louis Dreyfus, sources said, while December feedpeas closed down US$0.90 at US$211.10.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
